claims.evidence: Witness photos show a dismantled car engine/transmission assembly with bellhousing and circular cover plate, but no readable make/model/part number tying it to Ford Fusion or 'American Drive'.
Photos do not show engine markings, cylinder count label, or readable engine type details.
No documentation, shipping marks, or serial/label readable in the photos to confirm origin.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Witness reports the assembly appears dismantled and dusty/dirty with loose components scattered; photos show no test evidence (no start/run/gear engagement) and no proof of 'never opened' or 'no knock'.
No readable engine capacity information is visible in the photos.

risks.risk: Not actually complete (missing key accessories/sensors/wiring harness/starter/alternator/related components), which can make it unusable or costly to rebuild.
risks.proof: A full laid-out inventory photo/clip showing every included component (starter, alternator, sensors, wiring harness, turbo/AC parts if applicable, mounting bolts/hardware) with labels, plus a close-up of connectors and mounting points.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as dismantled/possibly incomplete and not guaranteed working.

risks.risk: Internal damage or poor condition (e.g., worn bearings, cracked casing, bent shafts) not visible from external bellhousing/cover plate views.
risks.proof: A video clip of the unit being started and running (or at minimum spun/bench-tested) showing oil pressure/idle stability, plus a gear engagement test (forward/reverse) if it’s a gearbox.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case as not proven working / potential internal fault.

risks.risk: Unknown engine type (diesel vs petrol) and compatibility mismatch with Ford Fusion / the claimed gearbox/engine pairing.
risks.proof: Clear close-ups of engine identification plate/engine code and gearbox code/label (serial/part numbers), plus the exact matching part numbers shown on both units.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as compatibility-uncertain and treated as a generic dismantled assembly.

risks.risk: Leakage or contamination (oil/coolant leaks, water ingress) that would affect reliability but isn’t shown in the photos.
risks.proof: Close-up inspection photos of gasket surfaces, bellhousing area, and any wetness/staining, plus a wipe-and-check clip showing no fresh leaks after a short run/test.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially leaking/dirty with no reliability guarantee.

risks.risk: Condition may be worse than implied (photos suggest dismantled state and heavy dirt; could indicate long storage or prior failure).
risks.proof: A clean, well-lit walkthrough video showing the full assembly surfaces, casing condition, and any corrosion/cracks, with a timestamp.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case as used/dismantled with unknown storage history.

proof_requests: Send clear close-up photos of any engine/gearbox identification plates, engine code, and gearbox code/serial numbers (readable).
Send a video of the unit being tested: start/run (if engine) and gear engagement (if gearbox), showing no abnormal noises and stable operation.
Send photos/video showing the full list of included parts (starter, alternator, sensors, wiring harness, mounting bolts/hardware, any turbo/AC components if present).
Send close-ups of gasket surfaces and bellhousing area to check for cracks, missing seals, or leak evidence.
Provide any proof of origin (Belgium) such as shipping documents, labels, or receipts with matching serial numbers.
response.reason: The witness can confirm it’s a dismantled car engine/transmission assembly, but the seller’s key compatibility and working-condition claims are not supported by the photos and there is no test evidence. Without readable IDs and proof of working/test/complete parts, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set confidently.
